# Console commands

<!-- Generated by `coney-tools console render` from the console's catalogs. Do not edit. -->

Every built-in command of the [Coney console](console.md): the terminal F8 will open in the game. The page is generated
from `src/console/commands.toml` (the player set, in every build, the release build included) by `coney-tools console
render`; edit that file, never this page. The console's core is built; its front end and the commands' handlers are
planned, and a command whose handler is not registered is unknown when typed ([What is built](console.md#built)). The
set is the design's proposal, which a maintainer confirms ([The release set](studio/console.md#release-set)).

How to read an entry: the syntax line names each argument, `<required>` or `[optional]`; the **scope** says whose game
it touches (**local**: this machine's; **session**: the game everyone in a network session plays, which only the host
may change), and whether it **runs at once** or **waits for the step boundary** (between two simulation steps, in the
order lines were entered); **needs** is what must exist for it to run; **waits for** names the Coney feature without
which the command is absent. Each example shows a line as typed (after `>`) and the lines it prints.

19 commands.

| Command | Group | Access | Scope | Does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`help`](#help) | The terminal | player | local | Lists the commands this build and the running mods offer, by group, or one command's arguments and help. |
| [`clear`](#clear) | The terminal | player | local | Empties the terminal's output. |
| [`version`](#version) | The terminal | player | local | Coney's version and build, the SDK level, the disc's region and the renderer. |
| [`quit`](#quit) | The game | player | local | Ends the game through its normal exit, as closing the window does. |
| [`where`](#where) | The game | player | local | The level, the checkpoint, the step and the play time, as the run log stamps them. |
| [`bugreport`](#bugreport) | The game | player | local | Writes the last 30 s of the run log, every level, into the log file and says where. |
| [`settings`](#settings) | Settings | player | local | Lists the settings with their values. |
| [`get`](#get) | Settings | player | local | Reads a setting. |
| [`set`](#set) | Settings | player | local | Changes a setting for this session only; nothing is written to a file. |
| [`missions`](#missions) | Levels and missions | player | local | The missions the active profile has completed, with their checkpoints. |
| [`mission`](#mission) | Levels and missions | player | session | Starts a mission you have completed, at one of its checkpoints, as the mission select does. |
| [`log`](#log) | Panels and profiling | player | local | Opens the Log panel, filtered when given a filter. |
| [`resmon`](#resmon) | Panels and profiling | player | local | Opens the Resources panel: one row per running mod. |
| [`perf`](#perf) | Panels and profiling | player | local | Opens the Performance panel: the frame, the steps and the profiler's zones. |
| [`net`](#net) | Panels and profiling | player | local | Opens the Network panel: the session's link and its figures. |
| [`profiler`](#profiler) | Panels and profiling | player | local | Records a profiler capture of some frames, says how far it got, or writes it to the captures folder. |
| [`host`](#host) | Network play | player | session | Hosts a network game. |
| [`connect`](#connect) | Network play | player | session | Joins a network game. |
| [`disconnect`](#disconnect) | Network play | player | local | Leaves the network session: on a guest as the Player 2 quit, on the host by ending the session. |

## help {#help}

```text
help [command]
```

Lists the commands this build and the running mods offer, by group, or one command's arguments and help.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `command` | command | none (optional) | A command to describe |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** none: a reading

```text
> help where
where
  The level, the checkpoint, the step and the play time, as the run log stamps them.
```

## clear {#clear}

```text
clear
```

Empties the terminal's output.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** none

```text
> clear
```

It prints nothing.

## version {#version}

```text
version
```

Coney's version and build, the SDK level, the disc's region and the renderer.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** none: a reading

```text
> version
Coney 0.1.0 (release build)
disc: NTSC-U; renderer: gl3
```

## quit {#quit}

```text
quit
```

Ends the game through its normal exit, as closing the window does.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, waits for the step boundary
- **Doubles:** Closing the window, the menus

```text
> quit
quitting
```

## where {#where}

```text
where
```

The level, the checkpoint, the step and the play time, as the run log stamps them.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Needs:** a game in play
- **Doubles:** none: a reading; the PCSX2 recipe of the same name reads the same in the original

```text
> where
level 87, checkpoint 2, step 5400 (03:00.0)
```

## bugreport {#bugreport}

```text
bugreport
```

Writes the last 30 s of the run log, every level, into the log file and says where.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** The debug menus' Time page, which the release build lacks

```text
> bugreport
bug report: 412 lines written to coney.log
```

## settings {#settings}

```text
settings
```

Lists the settings with their values.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** The options and the player's command line

```text
> settings
fps_cap   60
show_fps  off
vsync     on
```

## get {#get}

```text
get <setting>
```

Reads a setting.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `setting` | setting | required | A setting's name: settings lists them |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** The options

```text
> get vsync
vsync on
```

## set {#set}

```text
set <setting> <value>
```

Changes a setting for this session only; nothing is written to a file.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `setting` | setting | required | A setting's name: settings lists them |
| 2 | `value` | text | required | Its new value, as the setting takes it |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, waits for the step boundary
- **Doubles:** The options and --fps-cap, --vsync, --show-fps and the other player options

```text
> set fps_cap 60
fps_cap 60 (for this session)
```

## missions {#missions}

```text
missions
```

The missions the active profile has completed, with their checkpoints.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Needs:** an active profile
- **Waits for:** the Coney feature `mission-select`; absent until it is built
- **Doubles:** The original's mission select

```text
> missions
1  checkpoints 1-3
2  checkpoints 1-2
```

## mission {#mission}

```text
mission <mission> [checkpoint]
```

Starts a mission you have completed, at one of its checkpoints, as the mission select does.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `mission` | mission | required | A completed mission's number in the story |
| 2 | `checkpoint` | checkpoint | `1` | One of that mission's checkpoints |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** session, waits for the step boundary
- **Needs:** a game in play, an active profile
- **Waits for:** the Coney feature `mission-select`; absent until it is built
- **Doubles:** The mission select

```text
> mission 3 2
starting mission 3 at checkpoint 2
```

## profiler {#profiler}

```text
profiler <action> [frames]
```

Records a profiler capture of some frames, says how far it got, or writes it to the captures folder.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `action` | choice: `record`, `status`, `save` | required | What to do with the capture |
| 2 | `frames` | int | none (optional) | How many frames record takes |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, runs at once
- **Doubles:** none: a reading

```text
> profiler record 120
recording 120 frames
```

```text
> profiler save
capture written: captures/capture-1.json
```

## host {#host}

```text
host [port]
```

Hosts a network game.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `port` | int | none (optional) | The port to listen on (the default port when left out) |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** session, waits for the step boundary
- **Doubles:** --host, the player's command line

```text
> host 27615
hosting on port 27615
```

## connect {#connect}

```text
connect <address>
```

Joins a network game.

| # | Argument | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `address` | text | required | The host's address, with :port when it is not the default |

- **Access:** player; **scope:** session, waits for the step boundary
- **Doubles:** --join, the player's command line

```text
> connect 192.168.1.20
connecting to 192.168.1.20
```

## disconnect {#disconnect}

```text
disconnect
```

Leaves the network session: on a guest as the Player 2 quit, on the host by ending the session.

- **Access:** player; **scope:** local, waits for the step boundary
- **Doubles:** The pause menu's Player 2 quit, closing the window

```text
> disconnect
left the network session
```
